name: Cabbage
grown_as: Hearting cabbage. ⚠️ CHECK: William's records list two red ball cabbages ('Red Drumhead', 'Mammoth Red Rock') and a green pointed spring cabbage ('Durham Early'). Drawn as a green round-headed cabbage, the most typical; for red, the leaves would be purple-blue (plum) with a grey bloom.
habit: A short, thick stem 10 to 20 cm with a ring of large, spreading outer leaves 50 to 70 cm across round a dense, firm, round head 15 to 20 cm. A biennial: the next spring the head splits and a branched flowering stem rises 1 to 1.5 m.

leaf.arrangement: Alternate, spiralling on the short stem; the inner leaves folded tightly over each other to make the head
leaf.outline: Outer leaves broad, rounded to obovate, 25 to 40 cm
leaf.base: Narrowing into a thick stalk; the lower part of the blade sometimes with a few small lobes along the stalk
leaf.margin: Smooth to shallowly scalloped and wavy, no sharp teeth
leaf.veins: A thick pale midrib and strong pale side veins branching out, raised beneath
leaf.surface: Hairless and smooth, with a waxy grey bloom that makes water bead up; the head leaves smooth and shiny
leaf.stalk: Thick, pale and short on the outer leaves, none on the head leaves
leaf.colour: Blue-green to grey-green; the head paler green

flower.form: A cross-shaped flower of four petals
flower.petals: Four, free, broad and rounded with a long narrow claw, spreading flat
flower.centre: Six stamens, four long and two short, with yellow anthers, round a green style
flower.behind: Four narrow upright green sepals hugging the petal claws
flower.carried: In long, loose spikes on a tall branched stem; the closed buds stay above the open flowers at the top of each spike

fruit: Long, slender pods 5 to 10 cm, cylindrical with slight bumps over the seeds, ending in a short beak 0.5 to 1 cm, spreading upwards along the stems. Green, drying straw-brown and splitting from the bottom to show a pale papery partition. Seeds round, 2 mm, dark red-brown to grey-black.
seedling: Two kidney-shaped seed leaves on short stalks, broader than long with a notch at the tip, like a heart with the stalk at its point, waxy grey-green; the first true leaves oval to round on long stalks, waxy blue-green with wavy edges.
winter: Winter and spring varieties stand through the cold as heads; others are cut before winter.

leaf: a broad rounded blade with a wavy, scalloped edge, no sharp teeth
a thick pale midrib and strong pale side veins
bloom: four pale yellow rounded petals in a cross
narrow upright sepals hugging the claws
closed buds above the open flowers
seed: round dark red-brown to grey-black seed 2 mm
seedling: two kidney-shaped seed leaves notched at the tip
the first true leaf oval on a stalk
young: a short stem with broad rounded waxy leaves on stalks
crop: a firm round head of tightly folded smooth leaves
a ring of broad spreading blue-green outer leaves with pale veins
flower: a tall branched flowering stem rising from the split head
pale yellow four-petalled flowers in long spikes
small bluish leaves clasping the stem
seedhead: long slender pods with short beaks along tall stems

look_alikes: Savoy cabbage has deeply blistered leaves. Kale makes no head. All the cabbage-family crops (cabbage, cauliflower, broccoli, sprouts, kale) are one species and share the waxy blue-green leaf; they differ in what is eaten. Swede and oilseed rape have bluish clasping stem leaves but their young leaves are hairy. Turnip and pak choi (Brassica rapa) have bright yellow flowers held above their buds.
